## Active

### D-099 — WELL_KNOWN_LAYERS and the template file list moved to blong-lib

> _2026-09-12 · core/blong-lib · active_

`WELL_KNOWN_LAYERS` and `listTemplateFiles` now live in `@feasibleone/blong-lib` behind the subpath
exports `./layers` and `./template`, and gogo re-exports `src/template-files.ts` unchanged so
`copy-template.mjs` and `kopi.ts` keep working. `**/.tap/**` was added to the ignore list at the
same time, because it was leaking hundreds of coverage files into every scaffolded realm.

### D-1016 — The perf toolkit is a library utility, so it lives in blong-lib and not in blong

> _2026-11-25 · core/blong-lib · active_

The perf toolkit lives at `@feasibleone/blong-lib/perf` rather than in `@feasibleone/blong`. The
blong package is the framework's type surface — it is what a realm imports for `handler`, the
runtime interfaces and the schema builders — so a measurement module beside `types.ts` made a
package whose contract is declarations also a home for report code, and its `./stream` and `./blob`
subpaths are the last of that kind rather than a precedent for more. `core/blong-lib` is the
repository's utility package (merge, ids, yaml, template scaffolding), it already exports one
subpath per file, and it depends on no framework package, which is what a module built on node
builtins should look like.

`@feasibleone/blong-allure` was the other candidate and is rejected: it is the writer the ttk engine
hands results to, so a sampler and a histogram there would make a measurement toolkit depend on a
reporting backend, while `perfWrite` writes the Allure attachment itself and imports nothing from
allure. The five pieces stand as they were decided: a sample set, a summary, a histogram, a text
report and an SVG chart, with `perfWrite` putting both files on disk and a result of the report's
own tagged `perf`, because a perf run is not a step result.
